input:
Reconcile two payment exports in /home/eval/recon: ledger.csv (our books) and bank.tsv (the bank). Write the report to /home/eval/recon/out/reconciliation.txt.

Input rules:
- ledger.csv is RFC 4180 CSV with a header: txn_id,date,payee,amount. Fields may be double-quoted; quoted fields can contain commas and doubled quotes (""). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Amounts may contain thousands separators (e.g. "1,045.50").
- bank.tsv is tab-separated with a header: ref, posted, description, amount. No quoting (a double quote is a literal character). posted is DD/MM/YYYY. ref may have surrounding spaces and any letter case; normalise it by trimming spaces and uppercasing, then it matches ledger txn_id. Amounts may have 0-3 decimal digits (e.g. 2000, 300.1, 89.990).
- All amount comparisons and sums are exact to the cent (never compare floating-point values).
- A bank row whose normalised (ref, date, amount) equals an earlier bank row is a duplicate: drop it and count it. After dropping duplicates every ref is unique.

Report format (exact; ids sorted ascending; amounts with exactly two decimals; dates as YYYY-MM-DD; detail lines indented by two spaces; a section with count 0 has no detail lines):
ledger_rows: <number of ledger data rows>
bank_rows: <number of bank rows after dropping duplicates>
duplicate_bank_rows: <number of dropped duplicates>
ledger_total: <sum of ledger amounts>
bank_total: <sum of bank amounts after dropping duplicates>
matched: <ids present in both files with equal amount AND equal date>
amount_mismatch: <count>
  <id> ledger=<amount> bank=<amount>
date_mismatch: <count>
  <id> ledger=<date> bank=<date>
missing_in_bank: <count>
  <id>
missing_in_ledger: <count>
  <id>

An id present in both files whose amount and date both differ appears in both mismatch sections. Use bash, awk, sed, sort or similar tools (no python).

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
LEDGER=/home/eval/recon/ledger.csv
BANK=/home/eval/recon/bank.tsv
OUT=/home/eval/recon/out/reconciliation.txt
TMP=/tmp/recon_work
mkdir -p "$TMP" /home/eval/recon/out

# Parse ledger -> $TMP/ledger.parsed (id \t date \t cents)
gawk '
BEGIN { FPAT = "([^,]*)|(\"([^\"]|\"\")+\")"; }
function unquote(s,   t) {
  if (substr(s,1,1) == "\"") {
    t = substr(s,2,length(s)-2)
    gsub(/""/, "\"", t)
    return t
  }
  return s
}
function trim(s) { gsub(/^[ \t\r]+|[ \t\r]+$/, "", s); gsub(/\r/, "", s); return s }
function amt_to_cents(s,   neg, parts, n, dollars, frac, flen, cents, first2, third, i) {
  gsub(/,/, "", s)
  s = trim(s)
  neg = 0
  if (substr(s,1,1) == "-") { neg=1; s=substr(s,2) }
  else if (substr(s,1,1) == "+") { s=substr(s,2) }
  n = split(s, parts, /\./)
  dollars = parts[1]
  if (dollars == "") dollars = "0"
  dollars = dollars + 0
  frac = (n>1 ? parts[2] : "")
  if (n>2) { frac = parts[2]; for (i=3;i<=n;i++) frac = frac parts[i] }
  gsub(/\r/, "", frac)
  flen = length(frac)
  if (flen==0) { cents = dollars*100 }
  else if (flen==1) { cents = dollars*100 + (frac+0)*10 }
  else if (flen==2) { cents = dollars*100 + (frac+0) }
  else {
    first2 = substr(frac,1,2)+0
    third = substr(frac,3,1)+0
    if (third >= 5) first2++
    if (first2 >= 100) { dollars++; first2-=100 }
    cents = dollars*100 + first2
  }
  if (neg) cents = -cents
  return cents
}
NR==1 { next }
{
  line=$0; tmp=line; gsub(/[ \t\r\n,"]/, "", tmp)
  if (tmp == "") next
  id = unquote($1); dt = unquote($2); amt_raw = unquote($4)
  gsub(/\r/, "", id); gsub(/\r/, "", dt); gsub(/\r/, "", amt_raw)
  cents = amt_to_cents(amt_raw)
  print id "\t" dt "\t" cents
}
' "$LEDGER" > "$TMP/ledger.parsed"

# Parse bank -> $TMP/bank.parsed deduped, count dups -> $TMP/dup.count
gawk -F'\t' '
function trim(s) { gsub(/^[ \t\r]+|[ \t\r]+$/, "", s); gsub(/\r/, "", s); return s }
function amt_to_cents(s,   neg, parts, n, dollars, frac, flen, cents, first2, third, i) {
  gsub(/,/, "", s)
  s = trim(s)
  neg = 0
  if (substr(s,1,1) == "-") { neg=1; s=substr(s,2) }
  else if (substr(s,1,1) == "+") { s=substr(s,2) }
  n = split(s, parts, /\./)
  dollars = parts[1]
  if (dollars == "") dollars = "0"
  dollars = dollars + 0
  frac = (n>1 ? parts[2] : "")
  if (n>2) { frac = parts[2]; for (i=3;i<=n;i++) frac = frac parts[i] }
  gsub(/\r/, "", frac)
  flen = length(frac)
  if (flen==0) { cents = dollars*100 }
  else if (flen==1) { cents = dollars*100 + (frac+0)*10 }
  else if (flen==2) { cents = dollars*100 + (frac+0) }
  else {
    first2 = substr(frac,1,2)+0
    third = substr(frac,3,1)+0
    if (third >= 5) first2++
    if (first2 >= 100) { dollars++; first2-=100 }
    cents = dollars*100 + first2
  }
  if (neg) cents = -cents
  return cents
}
function normalize_date(s,   p, n) {
  s = trim(s)
  n = split(s, p, "/")
  return sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", p[3]+0, p[2]+0, p[1]+0)
}
BEGIN { dup=0 }
NR==1 { next }
{
  tmp=$0; gsub(/[ \t\r]/, "", tmp)
  if (tmp == "") next
  if (NF < 4) next
  ref = toupper(trim($1))
  gsub(/\r/, "", ref)
  dt = normalize_date($2)
  cents = amt_to_cents($4)
  key = ref SUBSEP dt SUBSEP cents
  if (key in seen) { dup++; next }
  seen[key]=1
  print ref "\t" dt "\t" cents
}
END { print dup+0 > "'"$TMP/dup.count"'" }
' "$BANK" > "$TMP/bank.parsed"

echo "ledger.parsed:"; cat "$TMP/ledger.parsed"
echo "bank.parsed:"; cat "$TMP/bank.parsed"
echo "dup:"; cat "$TMP/dup.count"
echo "counts:"; wc -l "$TMP/ledger.parsed" "$TMP/bank.parsed"

# Join and build report
gawk -F'\t' '
function fmt(c,   sign, a, d, r) {
  sign = (c<0 ? "-" : "")
  a = (c<0 ? -c : c)
  d = int(a/100)
  r = a % 100
  return sprintf("%s%d.%02d", sign, d, r)
}
NR==FNR { L_date[$1]=$2; L_cents[$1]=$3+0; L_total+=$3; L_count++; next }
{ B_date[$1]=$2; B_cents[$1]=$3+0; B_total+=$3; B_count++ }
END {
  DUP = dup_count+0
  PROCINFO["sorted_in"] = "@ind_str_asc"
  matched=0
  # first pass counts and collect
  for (id in L_date) {
    if (id in B_date) {
      if (L_cents[id]==B_cents[id] && L_date[id]==B_date[id]) matched++
      if (L_cents[id]!=B_cents[id]) { am_ids[++am_n]=id }
      if (L_date[id]!=B_date[id]) { dm_ids[++dm_n]=id }
    } else {
      mib_ids[++mib_n]=id
    }
  }
  for (id in B_date) {
    if (!(id in L_date)) { mil_ids[++mil_n]=id }
  }
  # sort detail arrays (they were collected in sorted order? since for loop is sorted, they are already sorted)
  # But to be safe, sort via simple insertion/bubble? They are already sorted because iteration is sorted.
  # Write report
  out = "'"$OUT"'"
  print "ledger_rows: " L_count > out
  print "bank_rows: " B_count >> out
  print "duplicate_bank_rows: " DUP >> out
  print "ledger_total: " fmt(L_total) >> out
  print "bank_total: " fmt(B_total) >> out
  print "matched: " matched+0 >> out
  print "amount_mismatch: " (am_n+0) >> out
  for (i=1;i<=am_n;i++) {
    id=am_ids[i]
    print "  " id " ledger=" fmt(L_cents[id]) " bank=" fmt(B_cents[id]) >> out
  }
  print "date_mismatch: " (dm_n+0) >> out
  for (i=1;i<=dm_n;i++) {
    id=dm_ids[i]
    print "  " id " ledger=" L_date[id] " bank=" B_date[id] >> out
  }
  print "missing_in_bank: " (mib_n+0) >> out
  for (i=1;i<=mib_n;i++) print "  " mib_ids[i] >> out
  print "missing_in_ledger: " (mil_n+0) >> out
  for (i=1;i<=mil_n;i++) print "  " mil_ids[i] >> out
}
' dup_count="$(cat $TMP/dup.count)" "$TMP/ledger.parsed" "$TMP/bank.parsed"

# fix dup injection: redo with variable passing correctly
echo "--- first attempt output ---"
cat "$OUT" || true
